Theses.title: Three Theses
Theses.side: What I keep testing in real projects

items.title: Read the scenario before the model
items.body: LLMs are good at complex, ambiguous, data-rich problems. For real-time, zero-tolerance or high-volume simple tasks, use rules, smaller models or people. Place the task first; then choose the model.

items.title: Write the standard before the effect
items.body: AI quality isn't intuitive. Define success, failure handling and sampling first, then report with metrics. A high benchmark score doesn't mean the product works.

items.title: Engineering depth is about trade-offs
items.body: Ten years of engineering taught me where a plan starts to get complicated. I translate model capability into cost, risk and delivery pace, so algorithm and engineering teams can decide together.

AboutPage.title: About Me - Max Zhang
AboutPage.heading: About Me
intro: I'm Max, an AI product manager with 10+ years of full-stack engineering. In the past two years I led multi-agent systems from zero to production.

An engineering background makes me ask about boundaries first: who it's for, what counts as done, how failure is caught. I now apply that to AI products — from task definition and workflow design to evaluation and cost.
This site is my knowledge map and case library: 4 stages, 13 modules, six industry cases. Not a tutorial — the set of judgments I keep calling on when building AI products.
AboutPage.storiesTitle: Engineering Base: Three Things I Built

stories.title: An agent workflow for ad asset production
stories.background: A hundred thousand videos and 30,000+ images per month, produced through a manual, serial workflow.
stories.decision: Instead of asking the model to 'generate everything', we split planning, generation and review into orchestrated tasks with clear boundaries.
stories.action: Designed the multi-agent collaboration and sandboxed execution environment, integrated MCP tools, and defined task handoffs and failure fallbacks.
stories.result: 80%+ cross-team efficiency gain; cost per video later dropped to RMB 0.5–1.

stories.title: An AI-native engineering workflow
stories.background: High video generation cost and a long, repetitive path from requirement doc to bug fix.
stories.decision: Standardize inputs and outputs first, then let Codex, Claude and in-house MCP share the repetitive work.
stories.action: Connected requirement generation, task breakdown, execution validation and bug fixing into one loop.
stories.result: Reduced cost per video from RMB 2.5–3 to RMB 0.5–1.

stories.title: A digital platform for ad operations
stories.background: Asset production, approval, delivery and data feedback lived in separate systems and depended on manual coordination.
stories.decision: Unify the state machine and data definitions first; automation comes after.
stories.action: Led platform build-out and aligned production, approval, delivery and data workflows.
stories.result: Supported 100,000 videos and 30,000+ images per month with 80%+ efficiency gains.

CasesPage.title: Case Studies
CasesPage.subtitle: Six industry cases from my own AI product work.
CasesPage.note: Each case records the key judgments, workflow and evaluation criteria of the time; numbers come from my project records.

cases.name: AI customer support
cases.context: E-commerce support sees high volume and mixed intents. I built a support agent for a headphone store.
cases.user: C-end buyers (pre-sales and after-sales), plus B-end merchants who need support systems.
judgments: Emotional escalation is independent of business intent: complaints, self-harm or violence go straight to a human.
Resolve pronouns and references before retrieval; an incomplete question retrieves the wrong knowledge.
Never carry the full conversation: tokens and attention both collapse.
flow: Query rewrite: clean, decompose, resolve references
Emotion and risk check → reply or hand off
cases.eval: Evaluation focused on three things: whether human handoff stayed under control, whether mis-answer complaints fell, and average response time in long conversations.
cases.reuse: Splitting a conversation into route, retrieve, answer and fallback applies well beyond support.

cases.name: AI meeting notes
cases.context: Meeting-note products are crowded and cheap. I started by questioning whether the demand was real.
cases.user: C-end: study notes and personal productivity; B/G-end: meeting systems and private deployment.
judgments: Users don't want a transcript; they want to know what to pay attention to.
Correct ASR homophones with a company dictionary before summarizing.
Decide the template before generating; structure then stays stable.
flow: Classify meeting type and pick a template
cases.eval: Regression checks focused on proper-noun correction, action-item recall and template consistency.
cases.reuse: Template first, dictionary second, generation last — works for any structured document generation.

cases.name: AI homework solver
cases.context: A tutoring company's homework app needed photo-based math search for grade 7, to understand student difficulties and support learning analytics.
cases.user: Enrolled middle-school students; 40% feel anxious about being accused of copying answers.
judgments: Experience first: show the solution, verify against the question bank in the background.
Cold-start the question bank with an authoring tool, not by collecting questions manually.
Tag abnormal inputs: not-math and not-a-question are separate classes.
flow: Compare answers; withdraw and use the bank answer if inconsistent
cases.eval: MVP target: 630 enrolled students use it 3+ times within three months; 20 uploads per minute.
cases.reuse: Answer first, verify later — useful when accuracy matters but waiting costs more.

cases.name: AI companion
cases.context: A 24/7 companion chat product with a persona called Lin Xu.
cases.user: People seeking emotional support and someone to talk to.
judgments: A persona is not a paragraph of copy: personality, memory, capability, interaction and ethics.
Turn the relationship into a 0–100 number, then map it to tone and behavior rules.
Crisis intervention is a requirement, not a bonus feature.
flow: Reply (≤100 characters; never reveal persona or chain-of-thought)
cases.eval: Retention wasn't tracked long-term; the relationship tiers and behavior rules are the most important thing to define first in this kind of product.
cases.reuse: Turning abstract experience (intimacy, trust) into executable numbers is a general design move for emotional products.

cases.name: AI medical consultation
cases.context: Healthcare is high-stakes. I turned consultation into a SOP with chief complaint, question guide, bounded follow-ups and RAG.
cases.user: Patients with initial consultation or triage needs.
judgments: RAG retrieves the consultation process, not just medical knowledge.
Cap the number of follow-up rounds or users drop off.
A fixed four-part output — complaint, history, diagnosis, plan — is what makes QA possible.
flow: Retrieve consultation templates (private knowledge base, topK = 1)
cases.eval: No online effect data; the 106-complaint question guide is the baseline for completeness.
cases.reuse: Process knowledge can be retrieved too — a counter-intuitive but useful RAG pattern.

cases.name: AI travel planner
cases.context: Group tours aren't personal, custom trips are expensive, and self-planning takes time. Users want a complete plan, not information.
cases.user: Individual and family travelers with different preferences for pace, budget and style.
judgments: Ask three multiple-choice questions first, turning fuzzy demand into executable constraints.
Cross-city transport must cite real trains or flights from tools; both directions are required.
Never judge by average score alone: one version improved the average while the share above 80 dropped.
flow: Hotel / food / dates / transport in parallel
Planner composes title, overview, day-by-day timeline, lodging, pre-trip tips
cases.eval: Eight dimensions scored 0/1/2, normalized; across two versions the mean went from 0.75 to 0.775 (30 → 50 samples), but the share above 80 fell from 66.7% to 40% — so I didn't judge by the average alone.
cases.reuse: A dimension-based rubric plus versioned iteration logs is the most reusable asset in plan-generation products.

CasesPage.ctaTitle: All six point to the same thing.
CasesPage.ctaText: Put model capability into a concrete scenario — then define the boundary, the evaluation and the fallback.
